questions.a: 'being' — after a preposition ('for'), the verb must be a gerund. A wrong answer 'to be' breaks the absolute preposition-gerund rule.
'to have been living' or 'to have lived' — the living precedes the believing → perfect infinitive. A wrong answer 'to live' loses the time-order.
'rewrite' — bare infinitive after 'made + object'. A wrong answer 'to rewrite' adds 'to' where causatives forbid it.

questions.q: Senior non-finite work: perfect infinitives ('to have done' — before the main verb's time), passive infinitives ('to be done'), gerunds after ______ ('insisted on going'), and the bare infinitive after make/let/help and sense-verbs ('I saw him cross the road').

Fill in the blank: Senior non-finite work: perfect infinitives ('to have done' — before the main verb's time), passive infinitives ('to be done'), gerunds after ______ ('insisted on going'), and the bare infinitive after make/let/help and sense-verbs ('I saw him cross the road').
Fill in the blank: Time-order first: 'He seems to have left' — the leaving ______ the seeming; 'to have + V3' flashes back.
What is Senior non-finite work? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Senior non-finite work: perfect infinitives ('to have done' — before the main verb's time), passive infinitives ('to be done'), gerunds after prepositions ('insisted on going'), and the bare infinitive after make/let/help and sense-verbs ('I saw him cross the road').

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Time-order first: 'He seems to have left' — the leaving precedes the seeming; 'to have + V______' flashes back.
What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Senior non-finite work?
questions.a: Students use 'to + V' after prepositions ('for to go'), miss the perfect-infinitive time-shift, and add 'to' after make/let ('made me to go').

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student selects perfect/passive infinitive forms by time-order and voice, uses gerunds after prepositions, and applies the bare-infinitive rules after causatives and perception verbs.
